title: Critical regression: right swipes fail to select items and cannot delete in edit mode
environment: Current Android phone build; Pixel 10 Pro XL running Android 17. Last known working build has not been identified.
reproduction_status: User-observed; not independently reproduced during backlog gathering
history: Initially recorded as a source-review candidate concerning the signed-distance fallback for slow right swipes.

Promoted to a critical user-reported regression after reports that right-swipe selection fails and right-swipe deletion in edit mode is unavailable. The report also includes failure with sufficient velocity.
reproduction: In shopping mode, swipe an item to the right with sufficiently high velocity to trigger its action.
Also try a slow rightward drag beyond half the delegate width, independently of the velocity trigger.
Observe that the item is not selected/checked as expected. The user reports that left swipes appear to work.
Enter edit mode and try the corresponding right-swipe action to delete an item; deletion is not possible.
actual: Right swipes fail to trigger item selection, including the reported velocity or distance triggers, and the right-swipe delete action is unavailable in edit mode. Left swipes appear to work according to the user.
expected: A deliberate horizontal swipe triggers the mode-appropriate item action when either its velocity-based threshold is met or its travel exceeds half the delegate width. Right swipes must select/toggle items in shopping mode and delete items in edit mode. Left-swipe behavior must continue to work.
impact: A primary one-handed shopping interaction is broken and item deletion through the intended edit-mode gesture is unavailable. Severity explicitly described as critical.
source_notes: SwipeHandler.qml computes signed distance as pressPosition.x minus position.x and compares it directly with the positive actionTreshold for the long-drag fallback. A rightward drag has a negative distance in this expression.

The velocity calculation uses absolute millimeter distance divided by timeHeld. Investigate this path separately: the signed-distance observation alone does not establish why the reported high-velocity right swipe also fails.

Direction is chosen using target.x, then passed through TextDelegate.qml's swipe animation before ShopView.qml handles the action. Verify event/grab handling, direction, and action delivery rather than assuming a threshold-only fix.
ShopView.qml routes edit-mode right swipes to itemModel.remove(index); other handled swipe actions toggle the checked state.
acceptance_criteria: A sufficiently fast right swipe triggers the shopping-mode item action without requiring travel beyond half the delegate width.
A slow rightward drag beyond half the delegate width triggers the action without depending on the velocity condition.
Both trigger paths work for right-swipe deletion in edit mode, with the correct item removed.
Existing left-swipe actions and checked/unchecked ordering continue to work.
Short, slow movements and cancelled gestures do not trigger unintended selection or deletion; preserve deliberate pullback behavior.
Animations return rows to a consistent state, and system Back gestures do not trigger item actions or leave stuck drags; coordinate with UI-007.
Add regression coverage separating direction, velocity-triggered and distance-triggered gestures, and shopping/edit modes.
Verify the one-handed gesture on the affected physical phone, not only through direct model calls.
open_questions: Which build last had working right swipes?
What swipe sensitivity is selected on the affected phone?
Does the row move right and animate back without an action, or does the gesture fail to acquire or move the row?
evidence: User critical-regression report in the QShopper development chat on 2026-10-28, specifying both velocity and half-delegate-width triggers and the inability to delete in edit mode.
